document: Alone Against The Frost Solitaire Adventure in Canadas Wilds (Glenn Rahman  Gavin Inglis) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

paragraphs.text:
The clever knots of the hunters foil your party’s best attempts. 
You have no choice but to wait where you are as a long, cold 
night begins.

Slumped  against  your  tree  in  the  half-light  of  dawn,  you 
open your eyes to see a group of tiny figures watching you. They 
stand only as tall as your thigh. You wonder if you are dreaming.

The  group  has  pale  gray  skin  and  over-defined,  almost 
sculpted features. Their lack of color makes them seem inhuman. 
They carry bows and cords with wooden balls attached—some 
sort  of  bolas?  They  wear  grotesque,  angular  ornamentation, 
made from what you hope are animal bones.

They  cut  you  free  from  the  tree,  but  immobilize  you  for 
transport.  Half-carrying,  half-dragging,  the  little  wild  men 
bustle your party away. You are chafed and bruised when they 
finally pause in a clearing.
